summary: Round 2, documentation-only transfer review at f441033dd734190b0adbbea190e09cf18f3445e2. Scope per user steering: prepare a Perlmutter clone and task handoff; no generation, build, benchmark or GPU results are in scope and none are approved. The transfer package under notes/sim10_stream_length_20261109 (README.md, TRANSFER.md, perlmutter-dataset.json, perlmutter-runtime.json, review-01/*, status.json) is present, internally consistent and does not overclaim. Verified from inspected files: all eight module SHA-256 values in perlmutter-runtime.json equal the SDF runtime_files in notes/sim10_100k_bd_sweep_20261109/validation.json; the five bigdata sizes in perlmutter-dataset.json sum to the stated 335606159580 bytes and each equals 10000 events x panels x 1 MiB plus headers, consistent with a 10k-only prefix; segment lists give 5+6+7+7+7=32 distinct panels 0..31; SDF medians 1.189/2.356/3.479/4.502 GiB/s quoted in TRANSFER.md match validation.json case pairs; the earlier 2.1884/2.1197 one-stream figures match the round-1 review record. TRANSFER.md correctly states Lustre is not Weka, the prefix is validated only to 10k with SMD describing 16263 events, bigdata full hashes and Configure shapes were not rechecked, no Sim10 fixture was found in bounded areas, native/GPU/MPI execution is unverified, and it lists the required runner adaptations (OMPI rank variable, CUDA mask before imports, srun/Cray MPI, path allowlists, Lustre/Slingshot counters, fsync/FADV_DONTNEED caveat). Benchmark code is unchanged from 21f56de88 (runner/support/campaign/audit identical to round 1). Round-1 findings SLN-01..04, BDS-02, BDS-08 are carried forward accurately in review-01/responses.md and remain non-blocking. Four new low, non-blocking documentation findings (TRN-01..04) concern unnamed hardcodes in the referenced writers (ten streams, frozen /sdf snapshot with inode checks, 36037 source events), the fail-closed ethtool NIC helper imported by runner.py, stale SDF-framed statements in README.md including a scheduler-log claim for a job that never started, and the dataset record's reliance on out-of-repo receipts. No required artifact for this preparation scope is missing; native tests and the 24 receipt tests are explicitly out of scope and recorded as not run.

findings.evidence: TRANSFER.md says the writer starting points 'contain SDF paths, source manifests, calibration receipts and stream assumptions' and tells the agent not to reuse the s005..s009 mapping or experiment/run IDs. It does not name the hard structural assumptions that will fail on the Perlmutter source: xtc_fixture.load_sources requires exactly ten streams and 36037 source events and a frozen /sdf SNAPSHOT whose manifest must byte-equal OLD_NOTES/manifest.json with inode/mtime check_stat (xtc_fixture.py:13-15,184-188,227,234-242); verify.py:132, repeat.py:48 and validate_repeat.py:51,107 all require ten streams and ten dgrams per event; fixture.py:164 and verify.py:122 require a calibration manifest hash. The Perlmutter source as described has five JF streams s004..s008 and no ancillary streams are listed, so the five-plus-five layout the writers and validators assume may not exist.
findings.requested_change: Add one sentence under 'Writer starting points' listing these specific hardcodes: ten-stream/36037-event source contract, frozen SNAPSHOT manifest equality and inode check_stat, ten-dgram DataSource assertion in validate_repeat, and the calibration manifest hash requirement. State whether ancillary streams exist in mfx101232725 r0442 or that this must be determined in step 1. Documentation only.

findings.evidence: TRANSFER.md says Ethernet sysfs counters may miss Lustre traffic and that if counters are inaccessible the agent should retain local-cache evidence. The current code does not degrade: network_watch.physical_counters() raises 'No physical NIC counters available; refusing unobserved measurement' when no interface reports ethtool rx_bytes_phy/tx_bytes_phy (network_watch.py:16-31), and runner.py:54 calls it unconditionally before the cold gate, so on a node without those ethtool statistics the whole case aborts via comm.Abort. Likewise support.py imports plan_reads -> fixture_check with ROOT pinned to /sdf sample10_10k and jf_cold_ffb cache() rejects any path outside /sdf/data/lcls/drpsrcf/ffb/users/monarin (run.py:10,16). TRANSFER.md covers the allowlist port but not the fail-closed counter helper.
findings.requested_change: State explicitly that physical_counters()/counter_delta must be replaced or deliberately relaxed for Perlmutter, that the replacement must fail closed only on the agreed counter set, and that the import of plan_reads/fixture_check via network_watch must be severed or redirected. Documentation only; no code change in this transfer.
